beats.narration_slice: In 1900, sponge divers found a wreck off Antikythera.
beats.visual: A vertical technical-drawing scene of two sponge divers descending toward an ancient wreck scattered with amphorae on the seabed off a rocky Mediterranean island, framed by the recurring patinated-bronze bezel.
beats.purpose: show the discovery of the Antikythera shipwreck by sponge divers
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide underwater establishing view; two small descending divers above a diagonal wreck and amphora field; rocky seabed at lower third; cool deep-Aegean lighting with a pale shaft from the surface
beats.continuity: first subject-world image after the Flow opener, establishing the archaeological setting without carrying the host environment into it

beats.narration_slice: Its cargo included a corroded bronze lump.
beats.visual: A close technical illustration of a diver's hand lifting an irregular green-brown corroded bronze fragment from among broken amphorae and sediment, with the artifact isolated as the clear focal point.
beats.purpose: identify the unremarkable-looking corroded bronze object recovered from the wreck
beats.visual_fingerprint: tight artifact close-up; single gloved-free ancient-diver hand entering from upper left; rough bronze lump centered against broken pottery and sand; warm bronze glint against verdigris crust
beats.continuity: moves from the wide wreck discovery to one specific object within the cargo

beats.narration_slice: Inside were tightly packed, precision-cut gears.
beats.visual: An archaeological cutaway-style technical drawing of the bronze fragment opened visually to reveal a dense cluster of interlocking hand-cut bronze gears, with broken outer edges clearly distinguished from reconstructed internal geometry.
beats.purpose: reveal the compact precision gearing hidden inside the corroded fragment
beats.visual_fingerprint: extreme macro cutaway; interlocking gear teeth dominate the frame in layered depth; jagged fragment shell forms an irregular border around the mechanism; raking side light catches several tooth edges
beats.continuity: reveals the interior of the bronze object shown in the previous beat rather than merely reframing its exterior

beats.narration_slice: The mechanism was built over two thousand years ago.
beats.visual: A restrained Hellenistic workshop reconstruction in technical-drawing form: an ancient craftsperson's hands shape a small bronze gear beside dividers, bronze blanks and a partly assembled mechanism, with no modern tools or readable markings.
beats.purpose: place the mechanism's manufacture in the ancient Hellenistic world more than two millennia ago
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium overhead workshop view; hands and compass-like dividers at lower center; unfinished bronze gear blank offset right; partially assembled instrument upper left; warm ochre workshop glow over parchment
beats.continuity: shifts from the surviving internal gears to a historically grounded reconstruction of their ancient manufacture

beats.narration_slice: A hand crank moved pointers across astronomical dials.
beats.visual: A clean three-quarter technical reconstruction of the mechanism with one hand turning a side crank while linked gear trains visibly connect to slender pointers sweeping across concentric astronomical dials.
beats.purpose: explain that turning the hand crank mechanically drove pointers across the dials
beats.visual_fingerprint: three-quarter instrument view; crank projects from left edge and is actively turned; two pointers fan across a large circular face; exposed gear train visible along the right side; diagonal cause-and-effect composition
beats.continuity: advances from construction to operation by showing force entering through the crank and reaching the dial pointers

beats.narration_slice: One dial tracked the Sun and Moon.
beats.visual: A front-facing astronomical dial rendered as precise vellum linework, with distinct symbolic Sun and Moon indicators occupying different positions on the same circular path and restrained celestial arcs behind them.
beats.purpose: show that one dial represented the changing positions of the Sun and Moon
beats.visual_fingerprint: symmetrical face-on dial close-up; small radiant Sun disc at upper right and crescent Moon indicator at lower left; concentric rings centered vertically; sparse pale-blue orbital arcs with no labels
beats.continuity: zooms from the overall moving pointer system to the specific celestial bodies represented on one dial

beats.narration_slice: Others modeled cycles used to predict eclipses.
beats.visual: An abstract but historically grounded eclipse-cycle diagram built from nested gear-linked arcs: darkened Sun and Moon discs align along a crossing orbital geometry while a spiral-like cycle path curls around them without labels or numerals.
beats.purpose: explain that other dial cycles could be used to anticipate eclipses
beats.visual_fingerprint: diagrammatic oblique composition; eclipsed dark disc near upper third; crescent and solar symbols aligned on a diagonal; spiral cycle geometry sweeps from bottom right to top left; charcoal-heavy shadow emphasis
beats.continuity: moves from ordinary Sun-Moon tracking to a different modeled celestial cycle with a distinct predictive function

beats.narration_slice: Another tracked the cycle of major Greek games.
beats.visual: A separate circular cycle dial surrounded by restrained symbolic imagery of an olive wreath, stadium turning post and small ceremonial amphora, all integrated as unlabeled engraved motifs rather than readable text.
beats.purpose: show that the mechanism also tracked the recurring cycle of major Greek athletic games
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium circular-dial composition viewed slightly from above; olive wreath crowns the upper arc; stadium post silhouette sits lower left; ceremonial amphora sits lower right; bronze pointer crosses the center horizontally
beats.continuity: shifts from astronomical prediction to the mechanism's separate calendrical tracking of Greek games

beats.narration_slice: Inscriptions even explained parts of its operation.
beats.visual: An extreme close technical study of a surviving bronze plate fragment covered with shallow, densely packed but deliberately illegible incised marks, with a fine pointer indicating the relationship between the inscription-bearing plate and a nearby mechanical edge.
beats.purpose: show that explanatory inscriptions were physically present on parts of the mechanism
beats.visual_fingerprint: extreme close-up of pitted bronze plate at a steep raking angle; illegible incision texture runs diagonally; broken edge and one partial gear rim occupy the lower corner; narrow light grazes the etched surface
beats.continuity: moves from what the dials tracked to the physical evidence that the device included operational explanations

beats.narration_slice: It was a hand-powered mechanical model of the heavens.
beats.visual: A culminating technical illustration of the reconstructed mechanism suspended centrally against a restrained celestial sphere: the hand crank, nested bronze gears and pointers align visually with Sun, Moon and orbital arcs, making the machine read as a compact mechanical cosmos.
beats.purpose: summarize the Antikythera mechanism as a hand-powered mechanical representation of celestial motion
beats.visual_fingerprint: heroic full-instrument vertical composition; complete mechanism centered and slightly low; crank silhouette clear on one side; gears visible through a restrained cutaway; celestial arcs and two small heavenly bodies form a halo-like geometry above it
beats.continuity: pulls back from the inscription detail into a final integrated view that unifies crank, gears, dials and celestial cycles while remaining entirely inside the established world
